advances: Positive sampled fibers over arbitrary finite real bases; a feasible variation and fixed-cap derivative, without stationarity.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
At fixed $(z,u)$ the support $h_z(u)$ is the maximum of $\sum_p\alpha_p h_{K_p}(u)$ over convex representations of $z$. The maximum can be taken over the finite feasible affinely independent supports. The corresponding affine basis values have slopes bounded uniformly in $u$; along any line segment in $B$ the feasible simplices cut the segment into finitely many intervals. The optimal value is concave, and at their endpoints is continuous: compactness of the coefficient simplex gives upper semicontinuity, and mixing any maximizing representation of the endpoint with a representation farther into the interval gives the one-sided lower bound. The bounded basis slopes give a uniform Lipschitz bound in $z$ on these segments. Support functions of sections in a fixed bounded hull have a uniform Lipschitz bound in $u$, proving joint continuity. All sections contain balls of one common positive radius, by Minkowski combinations of the sampled inballs.

The constraints are closed and convex because $h_z(u)$ is concave in $z$. Convexity along rays and boundedness of $V$ for $(u,z)\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\times B$ and $\|x\|\le1$ imply a uniform lower bound $-L(1+\|x\|)$ on the field. Testing $u=x/\|x\|$ bounds $C_t$ in a common ball for small $t$. On this ball use a uniform bound $L'$ on $|V|$. At a fixed old fiber with inball radius $b$ about $c$, the homothet of ratio $1-tL'/b$ about $c$ is feasible in the new fiber, and the support bounds put the new fiber inside the old parallel body of radius $tL'$, hence inside the homothet of ratio $1+tL'/b$. This proves positivity and uniform $O(t)$ radial displacement.

At $x=c+\rho(\omega)\omega$ with unique normal $n$, any active constraint at the new radial endpoint has normal tending to $n$, by compactness and the old support inequalities. Here $n\cdot\omega$ is bounded below by the inradius divided by an outer radius. Testing the old normal gives the upper bound on $(\rho_t-\rho)/t$, and the equality at the new active normal with its nonnegative original slack gives the lower bound. Both converge to $-V(n,p,x)/(n\cdot\omega)$. Convex boundaries have unique support normals surface-almost everywhere by Lipschitz graph charts and differentiability almost everywhere. The radial map and its inverse are Lipschitz (the radial function is the reciprocal of the positive Lipschitz gauge on the sphere), so exceptional directions are null. Differentiate the radial volume integral by dominated convergence. Its surface Jacobian is $\rho^{d-1}/(n\cdot\omega)$, so the result is the asserted normal-speed integral. For a fixed cap, apply the same radial shell argument with its indicator, which stabilizes except on the surface-null cap plane. In dimension one the radial integrals use the two directions with counting measure.

Finally the minimum defining $m$ is concave as an infimum of concave functions, and the constraints with $u$-independent field are precisely its superlevel condition relative to $tV$. Inside a fiber, the minimum support slack is the largest radius of a centered contained ball. Outside, the nearest-point supporting plane gives the negative distance and no unit support direction can have larger violation by Cauchy–Schwarz. These identify the signed distance also at the boundary.
statement:
Let $P$ be a finite nonempty real base set, $B=\operatorname{conv}P$, and $K_p$ positive compact convex $d$-bodies, $d\ge1$, which are the actual sampled fibers of their lifted hull $C$. For $z\in B$ let $h_z(u)=h_{C_z}(u)$ for $u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$. For any jointly continuous field $V(u,z,x)$, finite and convex in $(z,x)$ for each $u$, define
$$
C_t=\{(z,x):z\in B,\ u\cdot x+tV(u,z,x)\le h_z(u)\text{ for every unit }u\},\qquad t\ge0.
$$
For small $t$ these are actual convex bodies in the same relative ambient space with positive sampled fibers $O(t)$ Hausdorff-close to the old ones. A field may in particular be a signed normal-dependent affine physical function plus any finite nonnegative combination of continuous nonnegative normal weights times finite continuous convex physical functions. With $\eta$ the summed boundary $\mathcal H^{d-1}$ marked by the unique outer unit normal at regular points, the right total volume derivative is $\int r\,d\eta$, where $r=-V$ on the regular boundary. For a fixed nonvertical cap $H$ whose boundary meets the body boundaries in a surface-null set, the right captured-volume derivative is $\int\mathbf 1_H r\,d\eta$. Use counting measure at the endpoints when $d=1$. For $V$ independent of $u$, the same family is given by $m(z,x)\ge tV(z,x)$, where $m(z,x)=\min_{\|u\|=1}(h_z(u)-u\cdot x)$ is concave and is the signed distance to the fiber boundary (positive inside).
title: Normal-dependent convex defining functions give actual finite-fiber variations
